description: Visas Mantis SAOs screen applicants against the Technology Alert List, which covers nuclear, missile, aerospace, materials, sensors, information security and related fields.
Iranian applicants are concentrated in exactly the engineering and physical science disciplines the TAL covers, so the screen catches a large share of the population rather than a targeted subset.
notes: Directionally well supported; needs a field-of-study breakdown to state as fact. Layer-5 target.

aspect: Renewal risk for people already inside
description: A student or worker already in the US who leaves the country must re-apply abroad and can be caught in a new SAO, stranding them outside a life they have already built. The rational response is to stop leaving - which means not attending funerals, weddings or a parent's illness.
energy_note: Self-imposed exile from one's own family while lawfully resident.
notes: Extremely common account; layer-5 target for documented cases.

aspect: EXAMPLE - a year of vetting, revoked in an afternoon
description: Shahab Dehghani's student visa was granted by the State Department after a year of intense vetting, and revoked by a CBP officer at the jetway. The two decisions used the same facts.
energy_note: One arm of government overruling another, at the door.

aspect: SCENARIO - the lab he had to leave
description: Omid's PhD is in computational fluid dynamics. His advisor moves the group's work onto a project with a turbomachinery sponsor. Legal review flags the sponsor's export classification. Nobody says the word Iranian; he is simply moved to a different sub-project, on a different timeline, away from the part that publishes.
energy_note: Reassigned politely, out of the work that builds a career.
